facts.text: Clarksville was founded in 1783 by George Rogers Clark at the only seasonal rapids on the Ohio River, making it the oldest town in the former Northwest Territory.
In 1805, the Indiana Territorial Legislature authorized a canal to bypass the Falls of the Ohio at Clarksville, a project that never materialized.
Clarksville hosts the Falls of the Ohio Fossil Site, where 386‑million‑year‑old Devonian coral reef remains are displayed in hands‑on exhibits.
The town’s historic roots include a 1778 post on an island at the head of the Falls, used by George Rogers Clark to train his regiment.
Clarksville’s name honors its founder, George Rogers Clark, whose brother William later became famous as a frontiersman and explorer.
The town’s riverfront is being transformed into parks, housing, and restaurants, preserving its historic character while offering modern amenities.
